title: 1.1 Definition of Robots — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: What counts as a robot under ISO 8373 and other definitions, how autonomy works, where the words robot and robotics came from, and how robots sense, think and act.

title: 1.2 History and Evolution of Robots — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How robots evolved, from ancient automata and Jacquard’s loom to Unimate, the 1970s firsts in Europe and Japan, mobile robots, cobots, ROS and today’s five million factory robots.

title: 1.3 Types of Robots — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How robots are classified: by structure (articulated, SCARA, delta, Cartesian, cylindrical, polar) and by application (collaborative applications, AGVs, AMRs, service robots and humanoids), with real spec sheets.

title: 1.4 Preliminary Requirements — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: What to know before programming robots: robot safety, Python, C++, vendor languages, math with a worked example, physics and electronics, Linux, git and simulators, networking, optional assembly and career paths.

title: 1.5 Common Applications of Robotics — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Where robots work today, with IFR 2025 figures: factories, warehouses, hospitals, farms, space and disaster zones, plus case studies from Mars, the World Trade Center, Fukushima and the first humanoid pilots.

title: 1.6 Robot Anatomy and Coordinate Frames — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How an industrial arm is built and measured: joints and degrees of freedom, gears and datasheets, accuracy versus repeatability, coordinate frames and the TCP, a worked kinematics example, singularities and blended moves.

title: 1.7 The Industrial Robot Cell — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: What turns a robot arm into a working cell: components, safeguarding and light-curtain distance, PLC-robot handshakes, integrator roles with FAT and SAT, three typical cells, cycle time and cost.

title: 10.1 Capstone: Build a Simulated Work Cell — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Capstone project: build a simulated pick-and-place work cell in URSim or ABB RobotStudio with gripper I/O, a safety configuration and a FAT-style test sheet, graded by milestones and a four-level rubric.

title: 10.2 Capstone: ROS 2 Pick-and-Place with MoveIt 2 — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Capstone project: build a pick-and-place task for a simulated UR5e with ROS 2, MoveIt 2 and the MoveIt Task Constructor on mock hardware or Gazebo, with milestones, tests and a rubric.

title: 10.3 Capstone: Speed-Controlled Wheel — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Capstone project: build an Arduino speed-controlled wheel with a quadrature encoder, H-bridge driver, PID loop and a state machine with ramps and a FAULT state, with milestones, safety and a rubric.

title: 10.4 Capstone: An Open-Source Cell Monitor — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Capstone project: build an open-source ROS 2 cell monitor that reads robot state, cell I/O and a camera check from stand-in servers, keeps a maintenance log, and is published with a real pull request. No hardware needed.

title: 2.4 Intro to ROS (Vendor-Agnostic) — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Discover why the Robot Operating System (ROS and ROS 2) is the universal middleware for robotics: from Willow Garage to DDS, ROS-Industrial, and vendor drivers.

title: 2.5 End-of-Arm Tooling and I/O — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How to choose and size grippers, mount them and set payload, and program the digital I/O that opens a gripper, confirms a grip and talks to a PLC, in URScript and RAPID.

title: 2.6 Your First Pick-and-Place — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Build a complete pick-and-place cycle in URSim (and RobotStudio): TCP and payload, a three-point fixture frame, approach offsets, exact stops at the grip, and re-teaching only three points when the fixture moves.

title: 2.7 Program Structure and Error Handling — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How robot programs are organized (RAPID modules and routines, URScript functions and threads) and how they recover from errors such as a missed pick, with a 3 by 3 palletizing loop.

title: 2.8 Vision-Guided Picking — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How robots use cameras to pick parts that are not in a fixed place: 2D versus 3D guidance, camera mounting, lens and hand-eye calibration, and the frame-shift math that turns a vision result into a correct pick.

title: 3.2 Your First Contribution — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: A guide to your first open-source contribution: non-code tasks, finding beginner-friendly issues in robotics projects, the fork and pull request flow, draft PRs, and communication norms.

title: 3.3 How Robotics Projects Work — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How major open-source robotics projects operate: ROS 2 release branching, stability rules, DCO sign-offs, build farm CI, and contribution norms across MoveIt 2, ros2_control, Gazebo, and Nav2.

title: 3.4 Lab: Your First Pull Request — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: A practical lab for making your first pull request to robOSStics: selecting an edit, submitting via the browser, local Git checks, and responding to review.

title: 3.5 Case Study: Contributing to Nav2 — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: A case study on contributing to the Nav2 mobile robotics navigation framework: core navigation concepts, plugin architecture, licensing, and community contribution processes.

title: 4.3 Installing ROS on Your Local Environment — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Master installing ROS 2 Lyrical Luth: Ubuntu 26.04 setup, Windows WSL 2 (including Windows on ARM), macOS options, environment sourcing, colcon build tools, and troubleshooting.

title: 4.4 Running Your First Example (Turtlesim) — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Drive Turtlesim, introspect topics and services, remap CLI arguments, set up a colcon workspace, and write custom Python rclpy publisher and subscriber nodes.

title: 4.6 Writing Your First ROS 2 Package — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Build a ROS 2 Lyrical Python package from scratch: workspaces and overlays, ros2 pkg create, setup.py and package.xml, rosdep, colcon, and a timer-driven node that drives Turtlesim in a square.

title: 4.8 Moving an Arm with MoveIt 2 — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Plan and execute arm motions with MoveIt 2 on ROS 2 Lyrical: URDF and SRDF, ros2_control mock hardware, move_group, OMPL and Pilz PTP/LIN, and a UR5e in RViz.

title: 4.9 ROS-Industrial and Vendor Drivers — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How ROS 2 drives real industrial arms: ROS-Industrial, the common driver pattern, and the UR, ABB, FANUC, KUKA and Yaskawa drivers, with real-time and safety limits.

title: 5.1 Ethics in Engineering — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Explore engineering ethics in robotics: NSPE and IEEE codes, ISO 10218:2025, ISO/TS 15066 collaborative safety, OSHA accident data, and EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230.

title: 5.4 Making a Robot Cell Safe — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: A practical integrator workflow for robot cell safety: the ISO 12100 three-step method, task-based risk assessment, guards and safety distances, performance levels, robot safety functions and lockout/tagout.

title: 5.5 AI in Robotics: Uses and Limits — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Where AI is really used in industrial robotics as of October 2026 (learned vision, predictive maintenance, LLM coding assistants, research foundation models), what the evidence says about AI-written code, and how to check it before it moves a real arm.

title: 6.10 Kinematics of a 2-Link Arm — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: The full math of a planar two-link arm: forward kinematics, the reachable ring, closed-form inverse kinematics with atan2, rounding edge cases, and the Jacobian singularity.

title: 6.7 State Machines — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How to organize robot behavior into finite state machines, implement non-blocking execution with millis(), and scale from IEC 61131-3 SFC to ROS 2 lifecycle nodes and Nav2 Behavior Trees.

title: 6.9 Motion Profiles and Interpolation — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How robots turn a target into smooth setpoints: trapezoidal, triangular and S-curve profiles, cubic and quintic time scaling, joint, linear and circular interpolation, zones, and time parameterization in MoveIt.

title: 7.1 Industrial Cameras and Optics — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Industrial camera hardware and imaging optics for machine vision: CMOS sensors, global versus rolling shutters, pixel size and resolution, lens parameters, f-number, telecentric metrology, and GenICam interfaces.

title: 7.2 Lighting for Machine Vision — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Industrial illumination techniques for machine vision: backlighting, ring and glancing lights, darkfield, diffuse dome lights, coaxial and in-line illumination, optical filters, and LED strobing.

title: 7.3 Image Processing Basics — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Core image processing techniques for industrial machine vision: color spaces, histograms, thresholding, connected components, blob analysis, Canny edge detection, and template matching.

title: 7.4 3D Sensing — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Principles of 3D machine vision for robotics: direct sensing versus inference, stereo triangulation, point cloud processing with PCL, planar segmentation, Euclidean clustering, and industrial picking requirements.

title: 7.5 Inspection and Measurement — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Automated machine vision inspection and dimensional gauging for robotics: spatial resolution, Nyquist limits, telecentric optics, distortion correction, presence detection, and barcode verification.

title: 7.6 Lab: A ROS 2 Camera Pipeline — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Build an end-to-end ROS 2 camera pipeline: camera driver concepts, sensor_msgs/Image, sensor_msgs/CameraInfo, image_transport, message synchronization, cv_bridge, and OpenCV processing nodes.

title: 8.1 From Wires to Networks — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Understand 24 V discrete DC I/O, sinking and sourcing circuits, NPN and PNP three-wire sensors, fieldbus networks, industrial Ethernet, cyclic and acyclic communication, and Device Level Ring resilience.

title: 8.2 Industrial Ethernet Protocols — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Explore industrial Ethernet protocols: EtherNet/IP and CIP, PROFINET RT and IRT, EtherCAT processing on the fly, Modbus TCP, and device description files (GSDML, ESI).

title: 8.3 Lab: Connecting a Robot to a PLC — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Connect an industrial robot controller to a PLC over fieldbus networks: EtherNet/IP implicit I/O, PROFINET modules, Modbus TCP register tables, URScript bit packing, and a Python pymodbus lab.

title: 8.4 Safety over the Network — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Understand functional safety communication across industrial networks: the black-channel principle, PROFIsafe, CIP Safety, Safety over EtherCAT (FSoE), and robot safety stop categories.

title: 8.5 From the Plant Floor to IT — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Connect shop-floor robotics to enterprise IT: IO-Link sensor technology, OPC UA address spaces and security, VDMA robotics and vision companion specifications, MQTT telemetry, and ros2_control.

title: 8.6 Network Design, Security and Diagnostics — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Design and secure industrial robot networks: ISA/IEC 62443 defense-in-depth, zones and conduits, DMZ architecture, VLAN configuration, Time-Sensitive Networking, and packet analysis with Wireshark.

title: 9.1 Preventive Maintenance — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Industrial robot preventive maintenance: maintenance strategies, inspection intervals, lubrication checks, battery replacement, control box cleaning, and torque verification.

title: 9.2 A Troubleshooting Method — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: A systematic troubleshooting methodology for industrial robot cells: lockout/tagout under OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147, symptom gathering, controller error logs, flight reports, and root-cause verification.

title: 9.3 Mechanical Problems — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Diagnose and service industrial robot mechanical systems: joint flat rings and seals, collision recovery and loose joints, electromechanical brakes, shaft alignment with flexible couplings, and dress pack cable retraction.

title: 9.4 Electrical and I/O Faults — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Troubleshoot electrical and I/O faults in industrial robot cells: multimeter verification of 24 V DC power supplies, sensor wiring protection, solid-state leakage, galvanic relay isolation, and industrial network diagnostics.

title: 9.6 Lab: Check a Robot's State from Python — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Query and control a Universal Robots controller remotely over TCP port 29999 with Python: robot modes, safety status, protective stops, and automated recovery without physical hardware.

title: Chapter 10: Capstone Projects — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Chapter 10 of robOSStics: four capstone projects: a simulated work cell, a ROS 2 pick-and-place, a speed-controlled wheel, and an open-source cell monitor that uses a little of everything.

title: Chapter 9: Maintenance and Troubleshooting — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Chapter 9 of robOSStics: preventive and predictive maintenance, industrial troubleshooting methods, mechanical wear and cable management, electrical and I/O fault finding, calibration and recovery, and remote state monitoring.

title: Chapter 8: Industrial Networks — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Chapter 8 of robOSStics: discrete I/O and fieldbuses, Industrial Ethernet protocols, robot-to-PLC communication, functional safety networks, plant-floor to IT integration, and network security.

title: Chapter 3: How to Contribute to Open Source — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Chapter 3 of robOSStics: open source licenses, public collaboration, repository anatomy, finding first issues, robotics project governance in ROS 2, MoveIt 2, ros2_control, Gazebo, and Nav2, and your first pull request.

title: Chapter 2: Robot Programming — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: Chapter 2 of robOSStics: online and offline programming, the RobotStudio and PolyScope environments, the URScript, RAPID and RRL languages, and an introduction to ROS.

title: Using This in a Class — Gerald Lê | robOSStics @ LSU
current: How to use robOSStics in a class or study group: chapter order, which chapter is optional, time estimates, quizzes as self-checks and the four capstone projects.

title: robOSStics — Gerald Lê @ LSU
current: robOSStics: a web-based course by Gerald Lê at LSU that teaches students to program robots, from robot types and applications to RobotStudio, PolyScope, URScript, RAPID, ROS and robot ethics.
